title: The call comes first
topic: In rural Texas emergency rooms with no trauma surgeon on call, the decision to transfer a badly hurt patient takes 15 to 30 minutes, and a UT Health San Antonio led team is building an AI tool that flags severe injury and prompts that call sooner, a tool still headed for a pilot.
hook: Nearest ER. No trauma surgeon on call.

treatment.logline: In a small Texas ER with no trauma surgeon, the first slow minutes come from one decision, and an AI tool under development aims to shrink that decision without making it for the doctor.
treatment.cold_open: Night. An ambulance swings into a small brush country ER and the doors bang open. Red light sweeps across the wall clock, its eyes snap open and a red wedge starts dragging behind the minute hand.
treatment.turn: A faster decision leaves the calls and the road untouched, and the survival benefit is only suspected. The tool drops into a drawer beside an ultrasound wand, just a tool.
treatment.button: The ambulance leaves down the same two-lane road while the wall phone hangs with its cord coiled short and rings again. The call could come sooner. The road is still the road.

hero.name: the ER wall clock with a face
hero.why: a round hospital clock whose eyes and brows act and whose face fills with a red wedge for every minute the transfer decision takes. It makes 15 to 30 minutes against 5 to 10 something a muted viewer can see, and no earlier film has drawn it.

throughline.object: the ER wall phone and its coiled cord

states.state: on its hook under her hovering hand, cord coiled and quiet
off the hook, cord stretched across the ER and out the door toward far hospitals
picked up early, cord barely uncoiled
back on its hook with the cord coiled short, ringing again

scenes.vo: A crash patient rolls into the nearest ER, and often there's no trauma surgeon on call. Often it's a Level Four center, a well equipped rural emergency room.

draw.subject: the ambulance
draw.action: swings in under the ER canopy and its back doors bang open as the gurney rolls out

draw.subject: the on call board by the door
draw.action: flips its TRAUMA SURGEON slot to an empty blank
draw.emotion: the doctor glances at it, uneasy

draw.subject: a sign
draw.action: swings down over the bay door reading LEVEL IV

scenes.vo: The doctor there treats everything from strokes to pediatric flu. Trauma is rarely her strength, because these towns don't see a lot of injury.

draw.subject: the doctor
draw.action: listens to a coughing kid's chest while the whiteboard behind fills with STROKE, FLU, FLU

draw.subject: the word TRAUMA
draw.action: squeezes onto the bottom of the whiteboard in small red letters

scenes.vo: First she has to decide to transfer. That decision alone takes 15 to 30 minutes today.

draw.subject: the wall clock
draw.action: snaps its eyes open and its minute hand starts dragging a red wedge

draw.subject: the red wedge
draw.action: paints a quarter, then half of the clock face as the clock sweats

draw.subject: the doctor
draw.action: hovers her hand over the wall phone still on its hook

scenes.vo: Texas has 173 basic Level Four centers, and only 22 at Level One.

draw.subject: the doctor
draw.action: pushes the gurney like a shopping cart down an aisle as low shelves fill with 173 small hospital boxes

draw.subject: 22 big hospital boxes
draw.action: light up on the top shelf, far out of her reach

scenes.vo: Then she has to hospital shop by phone for a trauma center that will take the patient, and call an ambulance.

draw.subject: the doctor
draw.action: yanks the wall phone off its hook and the coiled cord springs straight

draw.subject: the phone cord
draw.action: snakes out the ER door across the brush toward far hospital towers that shake their heads one by one

draw.subject: the last tower
draw.action: nods yes as the ambulance's light bar flicks on in the bay below

scenes.vo: After the yes comes the wait. State registry data show up to 80 percent of the most severely injured wait more than two hours to be transferred.

draw.subject: ten gurneys
draw.action: line up in a long hallway under a big clock

draw.subject: eight of the ten gurneys
draw.action: stay parked under the clock while two roll out the door
draw.emotion: the paramedic checks his watch, tired

draw.subject: the clock's hand
draw.action: spins around the face twice, leaving a red ring each lap

scenes.vo: The stakes are high. Trauma is the leading cause of death for people up to age 45.

draw.subject: a ruler of ages
draw.action: unrolls along the ground with a kid, a teen, a young ranch hand and a mother stepping onto it

draw.subject: a flag marked 45
draw.action: stakes into the ruler's end as everyone on it turns to look

scenes.vo: In San Antonio, trauma surgeon Brian Eastridge spent much of his career as an Army trauma surgeon in war zones. Now he co-leads iRemedyACT, a statewide team using AI on this delay.

draw.subject: a trauma surgeon
draw.action: walks into frame past a window with the San Antonio skyline

draw.subject: a field tent
draw.action: slides in behind him as a helicopter's shadow passes over

draw.subject: three researchers
draw.action: gather at a table as a banner drops and a statewide web of lines lights up behind them

scenes.vo: Their tool flags signs of severe injury and prompts an earlier transfer call. It pushes the doctor to make that decision sooner.

draw.subject: a small amber flag
draw.action: springs up on the tablet at the bedside and pulses

draw.subject: the doctor
draw.action: glances at the flag and reaches for the phone right away

scenes.vo: With the tool, that decision could take five to 10 minutes.

draw.subject: a pencil
draw.action: sketches a thin dashed wedge on the clock beside the shrinking red one

draw.subject: the phone cord
draw.action: barely uncoils as the doctor makes the call early

scenes.vo: A faster decision still leaves the calls and the ride. A survival benefit is something he suspects.

draw.subject: the ambulance
draw.action: drives a long empty two-lane road under the night sky, its lights sweeping the brush

draw.subject: a road sign
draw.action: swings up ahead stamped with a question mark as the paramedic at the wheel squints at it

scenes.vo: He calls it just a tool, like an ultrasound. It sharpens the doctor's judgment instead of replacing it.

draw.subject: the AI tablet
draw.action: slots into a supply tray beside an ultrasound wand that side-eyes it and a stethoscope

draw.subject: the doctor
draw.action: runs the ultrasound wand with one hand and taps the tablet with the other, then decides

scenes.vo: A UT System AI moonshot called BEACON plans to test an AI assistant at seven UT hospital sites. As of September, a statewide pilot of the transfer tool was planned for the fall.

draw.subject: seven hospital towers
draw.action: pop up in a row and light their windows one after another

draw.subject: a glowing assistant badge
draw.action: rises over the seven towers and beams a thin line down to each one

draw.subject: a paper tag
draw.action: swings onto the tablet in the surgeon's hand reading PILOT PLANNED in pencil

scenes.vo: The call could come sooner. The road is still the road.

draw.subject: the ambulance
draw.action: pulls away from the ER down the same two-lane road
draw.emotion: the doctor watches from the door, steady

draw.subject: the wall phone
draw.action: rattles on its hook in the foreground, cord coiled short, as the ambulance's tail lights shrink down the road through the door
